breakdown.claim: The FDA approved the first CAR-T therapy in 2017 for children with acute lymphoblastic leukemia.
breakdown.reason: The NCI source explicitly states that the FDA approved the first CAR T-cell therapy in 2017 to treat children with acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL).

breakdown.claim: The report states that six CAR-T therapies are FDA-approved for blood cancers: four target CD19 and two target BCMA.
breakdown.reason: The context explicitly states that there are six FDA-approved CAR-T therapies, with four targeting CD19 and two targeting BCMA.

breakdown.claim: All currently FDA-approved CAR-T products use second-generation CAR constructs.
breakdown.reason: The CAS source explicitly states that all currently FDA-approved CAR-T cell therapies are based on second-generation constructs.

breakdown.claim: The approved uses of two CAR-T therapies have expanded to second-line treatment for adults with some blood cancers.
breakdown.reason: The NCI source explicitly states that the approved uses of two CAR T-cell therapies have been expanded to second-line treatments for adults with some blood cancers.

breakdown.claim: Lisocabtagene maraleucel received accelerated approval for relapsed or refractory CLL/SLL after at least two prior lines of therapy, including a BTK inhibitor and a BCL-2 inhibitor.
breakdown.reason: The AACR source explicitly states that the FDA granted accelerated approval for relapsed or refractory CLL/SLL after at least two prior lines of therapy, including inhibitors of BTK and BCL-2.

breakdown.claim: In 65 evaluable patients in the TRANSCEND CLL 004 study, 25% achieved partial responses and 13 achieved complete responses.
breakdown.reason: The AACR source explicitly states that, of 65 evaluable patients, 25% experienced partial responses and 13 patients experienced complete responses.

breakdown.claim: For patients with partial responses in TRANSCEND CLL 004, response durability was 60.3% at 12 months and 46.9% at 18 months; among complete responders, the corresponding figures were 100% and 87.5%.
breakdown.reason: The AACR source explicitly reports these 12- and 18-month figures for partial and complete responders in TRANSCEND CLL 004.

breakdown.claim: Conference-reported rapidly manufactured CD19-directed CAR-T products had a median leukapheresis-to-delivery time of 9 days.
breakdown.reason: The conference summary explicitly reports that studies of rapidly manufactured CD19-targeting products found a median time from leukapheresis to delivery of nine days.

breakdown.claim: A phase I multiple myeloma study reported in vivo BCMA CAR delivery in four patients.
breakdown.reason: The context explicitly describes a phase one study in relapsed/refractory multiple myeloma with four patients, using in vivo delivery of a lentivirus carrying a BCMA CAR.

breakdown.claim: The ALPHA3 trial is evaluating allogeneic CAR-T therapy in lymphoma.
breakdown.reason: The Duke Cancer Institute source explicitly says ALPHA3 investigates allogeneic CAR-T treatments for high-risk patients with aggressive lymphoma.
